question: Which authored rule changes create missing-evidence obligations on the actual 50,931 saved procurement receipts under their archived structural-order retention masks?
analysis_type: Post hoc descriptive projection of existing authored targets onto the same exposed public archive; not new data, an independent holdout or observed organizational changes
cohort: Exactly all 50,931 saved old receipts; the actual retained observations and masks are joined to the same immutable source by unique case ID and checked against archived access traces
domain: Fixed cartesian:v1; all supported completions consistent with retained activities, profile if observed and exact first timestamps if observed; the old Boolean is not a hidden restriction on new completions
target_selection: Regenerate the original 80 single-edit targets from raw JSON grammar, recompute complete truth vectors, and independently derive exact semantic equivalence and all-profile satisfiability; match all four previously declared selection sets including the 39 satisfiable semantic representatives. Keep the two-edit strict anchor separate from every set.
class_mapping: First-occurrence activity order, observed block mask, retained profile and exact timestamp weak order determine the native observation class. Map to existing finite-census observation IDs without selecting on outcomes. Source values of unread fields never enter this class key.
outcomes: For each target and observed class, validate old sufficiency; classify safe, stale_verdict or insufficient and derive all minimal robust additional masks from opposed completions. Expand counts and IDs using native class membership, without changing saved retention.
affected_definition: Affected means insufficient and requiring source acquisition; stale-but-sufficient records are reported separately. Counts of affected target/case pairs, union distinct affected IDs and the number of targets with any affected records are never interchanged.
descriptive_summaries: For every selection set, report target count, status target/case pairs, P/T/PT requirements, distinct affected-ID union, affected native classes, targets with any affected records, and median/min/max per-target insufficient records both across all targets and conditional on nonzero workloads. These are descriptive dependent counts, with no population confidence intervals.
recovery: Simulate the previously used P-first adaptive logical block policy with actual archived values, stopping only when the new observation is sufficient. Compare the final verdict with direct raw complete-input evaluation. These counts exclude setup scans and are not measured physical I/O, latency or an advantage over ordinary recomputation using the same policy.
checks: Recompute raw old/new finite truth labels independently of candidate engines; compare all 80 native status/robust rows against existing full-census rows. Verify raw source literals, masks, receipt bindings, old sufficiency and native state support; separately recover the strict 33,489-ID anchor and the four weakening targets' 114 two-block cases and 199 adaptive reads, including exact per-target ID digests.
outputs: Deterministic native case-to-class mapping and insufficient target/case ID index in gzip JSONL, per-target class and aggregate summaries, selection summaries, independent checks, input/output SHA-256 pins and concise manuscript text. Hashes identify bytes and do not authenticate source truth.
replay: Run with a new output directory; deterministic evidence files must match byte-for-byte. Protocol timestamp and runtime are provenance only, not benchmark results. Existing scientific files are read-only.
